11:31pm A perfect game for GT. SRH were never really in, definitely not during the 
chase. Prasidh came in the powerplay and struck. His middle-overs bowling continued 
to be on point and he finished with 2 for 19 in a 224-run chase. Head fell for 20. 
Abhishek's 74 came off 41 balls. He wasn't at his fluent best but gave SRH some hope. 
Kishan was kept quiet. 
Pat Cummins, SRH captain: Our powerplay with the ball wasn't great, I was guilty there. 
We gave away 20 too many there. Had to hang on to our catches throughout the middle, 
i was guilty there. Maybe chasing 200 would've been more realistic. They're class 
batters in GT. They don't do anything outlandish. If you bowl bad balls they put it away 
and we did dish up many bad balls. But they're quality, know this venue well. We weren't 
at our best. It was a really good wicket, going for 140 off the last 14 was a good effort 
from our bowling group. Felt we were in the game with our batters. But in the end it was 
a bridge too far. Abhishek batted nicely, Nitish did well too. We left a bit too much for 
the batters. We have to cling onto some hope. Big auction last year. This group will be 
together for three years, hopefully, so lots to play for. Great venue, very few empty seats, 
crowd was nice and loud. 
Jos Buttler: Our best performance in the field. We've dropped a few this season, 
Rashid's catch set the tone. The guys at the top have been in great form. Openers have 
traditional techniques and can occupy the crease. They took us by surprise actually with 
how fast they scored with classical shots. Sudharsan has a great head on his shoulders. 
Blown away by how good he is. He puts in the work, understands his game well. He's 
shown great consistency and is getting the rewards he deserves. Prasidh does the 
basics well, bowls a fantastic line. Doesn't give width, watches the batters well, mixes 
his length nicely. He's disciplined with lengths when not bowling bouncers and yorkers. 
Fielding has been the big thing. Batting and bowling has been excellent. Going forward, 
catches are match-changing, if we tidy up there. MI are a form team, always a great 
game to play at the Wankhede. 
Shubman Gill, GT captain: (22 dot balls) Didn't plan that, idea was to continue to play 
like we have. Black soil, we've seen it's not easy to hit sixes. But the way our top order 
plays, we know how to keep the scoreboard ticking. (On GT's top-loading) We've never 
had the conversation for one of the top-three to always be there at the end. We're just 
eager to score runs and do our best. As a side, our fielding had been below average this 
season but it was great today. Everyone is chipping in - Prasidh, Ishant, even Coetzee - 
makes it easier defending a score. (On his chat with ump) There are so many emotions, 
you give 110% on the field, sometimes you're bound to show emotions. 
Prasidh Krishna, POTM and purple-cap holder: Purple cap doesn't feel any different. 
Winning was key. We've had two long breaks. Getting a win at home was important. My 
control over length has been good. Lots of support from the team to get where I am 
now. (Pre-match work and conditions assessment) Prep would start with controlling 
what I can in the nets. Do what I'd do during the game. On game day, you watch every 
ball of the first innings if you're bowling second. Take all that you can. Then have chats 
with the experienced players around, then hit the right areas and take it from there. I 
have a red ball in my room, playing around with it. Didn't get it to the ground. Looking to 
take this tournament first and then look at what's coming later.
